title: Buffer aliasing in prefill queue causes token-offset skew and softmax instability
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Users observed small but reproducible token misalignment and quality regressions (softmax instability) after we shipped the prefetch scheduling changes in runtime-1.22. The failure manifests as a 0.1%-1% change in token probability distributions on long-prefill+decode workloads and periodic off-by-one token insertions during multi-request concurrency bursts.

Hypothesis (initial):
A scheduling change implemented to improve throughput (staggered lane throttling and aggressive prefetch reuse) introduced a latent buffer-aliasing bug in the prefill queue. Concurrent kernel handoffs can now reuse a prefetch buffer slot before the previous writer has fully finished committing the KV index metadata. The result is two kernels writing overlapping KV/prefix buffers causing: (1) token index shifts (one request sees a stale tail from previous request), and (2) tiny numerical differences in softmax due to mixed-buffer reads leading to divergence over long sequences.

Impact:
- Reproducible on our internal long-shot test harness for the Llama-family-derived variants with sequence lengths > 1024 and concurrent prefill+decode pipelines.
- Causes correctness regressions (not just perf variance) — outputs diverge from baseline models and occasionally inject a duplicated token.
- Medium customer impact for apps that rely on deterministic outputs or long context coherence.

Reproducer (local):
1) Run long_prefill_decode_harness --model raf-small --seq 2048 --concurrency 8 --staggered-scheduler=true
2) Observe: token probability KL divergence vs baseline > 0.001 after 400 tokens and occasional token duplicates at token index boundaries.
3) Capture nvprof traces and runtime logs with PREFETCH_DEBUG=1 to observe overlapping buffer write timestamps.

Root cause (so far):
- Scheduler lane throttling introduced a fast-path that marks prefetch slots as "available" based on a write fence that only waits on kernel completion but not on subsequent metadata commit tasks scheduled on the CPU threadpool.
- Under high concurrency the CPU-side metadata commit can be delayed and a new prefill task reclaims the same slot (buffer alias) while stale meta still points at the previous request's KV extent. The kernel then reads a mixture of old and new KV fragments during attention, producing numerical drift in softmax and occasional token duplication.

Temporary mitigation applied: 
- Disabled staggered lane fast-path for models in canary pool (runtime-1.22-canary) to serialize prefill handoffs for affected models. This is deployed to a subset of hosts and reduces incidence to near-zero for canary traffic.

Logs and artifacts: 
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-142007+Prefill+Buffer+Aliasing+Investigation
- Reproducer harness: internal://harnesses/long_prefill_decode_harness (CI job ID: 2025-02-27-PR1426)
- Profiling traces: s3://redwood-artifacts/eng/ENG-142007/traces/
- Github PR (temporary mitigation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4879

Decision:
- Short term: keep canary mitigation in place and widen to Dedicated test pool while we validate the fix.
- Long term: rework prefill slot lifecycle to include a CPU-committed metadata fence that guarantees slot reuse only after all kernel + metadata commit tasks are observed as completed. Also add unit tests to simulate prefetch metadata commit delay and a stress test in CI.
comments: 2025-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Filed after root-cause triage during postmortem for nightly canary failures. Collected reproducer and initial nvprof traces.
2025-03-01 - Marco Ruiz: Confirmed reproducer locally. Observed overlapping cudaMemcpy timestamps in trace viewer; the write fence was returning earlier than expected under heavy CPU load.

2025-03-02 - Priya Nair (runtime): Added a synthetic stress test to CI that delays metadata commit by 5-20ms; that reproduced the token-shift failure 87% of runs. Filed a small mitigation PR to disable the fast-path for canary models.
2025-03-03 - QA: Deployed runtime-1.22-canary with mitigation to 10% of canary pool. No new token-dup reports in the canary window; latency regression <1%.

2025-03-04 - Eng lead (Bencho Wang): Agreed on design to add an explicit metadata completion fence and expand test coverage. Ownership assigned to Marco (kernel and scheduler) and Priya (meta commit path).

2025-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Working on deterministic unit test harness and a design doc for the fence. Prototype patch to runtime scheduler in branch eng/ENG-142007-fence pending review. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4895
